survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the publicly available PISA 2022 microdata for Vietnam (15-year-old students) and restricts the analytic sample to respondents with complete data on inquiry-based pedagogy and student math attitude (final N=5711). The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight procedure, and it does not name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate design (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the analysis is conducted via structural equation modeling in STATA, the paper does not document whether complex survey design features were incorporated into standard errors/fit indices. Analysts using the OECD PISA database should apply the appropriate student sampling weights and replicate weights when estimating uncertainty, especially given the nested sampling structure (students within schools) and the cross-regional disaggregation reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 Vietnam microdata for 15-year-old students in the mathematics major domain. From 6068 initial respondents, 357 were excluded due to missing responses on inquiry-based pedagogy, missing responses on student math attitude, or overlapping missingness; the final analytic sample contains complete information for both constructs. For math performance, the authors state there are no missing observations. The study then estimates a mediation model linking inquiry-based pedagogy (latent construct from a 7-item student questionnaire scale) to student math attitude (latent construct from a 5-item scale) and to math performance measured as a latent construct based on ten plausible values.

main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM mediation model: Direct effects std.β=0.084 (IBP→SMP, p<0.001) and std.β=0.072 (SMA→SMP, p<0.001); Indirect effect IBP→SMA→SMP std.β=0.030 (p<0.001). Model fit: χ2(296)=4280.65 (p<0.001), CFI=0.97, TLI=0.96, RMSEA=0.052, SRMR=0.058.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Vietnam (15-year-olds) Mathematics the study leveraged inquiry-based pedagogy (IBP) and student math attitude (SMA)—while controlling for socioeconomic status (ESCS), gender, and grade level—to model math performance (SMP), finding that IBP had a positive direct association with math performance (std.β=0.084, p<0.001) and that SMA also had a positive direct association (std.β=0.072, p<0.001), with a significant mediation pathway IBP→SMA→SMP (std.β=0.030, p<0.001). This indicates that strengthening inquiry-based instructional practices and simultaneously fostering positive student math attitudes may improve mathematics achievement in Vietnam, though the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 Vietnam mathematics data for 15-year-old students (final N=5711) to test a mediation framework linking inquiry-based pedagogy (IBP) to student math attitude (SMA) and then to math performance (SMP). Math performance is modeled as a latent construct based on ten plausible values, while IBP and SMA are latent constructs from student questionnaire Likert items. Using a PLS-SEM mediation model estimated in STATA, the authors report good overall fit (CFI=0.97, TLI=0.96, RMSEA=0.052, SRMR=0.058) and significant standardized paths: IBP→SMA (std.β=0.424, p<0.001), SMA→SMP (std.β=0.072, p<0.001), IBP→SMP (std.β=0.084, p<0.001), and the indirect mediation IBP→SMA→SMP (std.β=0.030, p<0.001). The paper uses listwise deletion for missing IBP/SMA responses and does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the cross-sectional SEM design constrains causal claims.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is an SEM-based mediation analysis rather than an empirical machine-learning prediction/classification study: it does not train or compare ML algorithms, and therefore ml_techniques are intentionally left empty. As a result, fields that would normally capture ML model selection (e.g., primary algorithm) are not applicable to the study’s analytic approach.
